llm.summary: The skill is plausibly a thin wrapper for a Google Workspace CLI (gws) to manage Google Tasks, but it defers authentication and security rules to an external shared SKILL.md that is not included — this missing dependency obscures what credentials or files will be accessed.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (Google Tasks) matches the required binary (gws) and the SKILL.md contents which document tasks/tasklists operations. Requiring the gws CLI is proportional to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions explicitly tell the agent to read ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules. That file is not present in this package listing. Instructing the agent to read an external/shared SKILL.md (or to run `gws generate-skills` to create it) grants the skill broad discretion to pull in auth logic and to create files — behavior that is not visible here and could change the security posture.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files are included (instruction-only), so nothing will be written to disk by the package itself. This is the lowest install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials in its metadata, yet it defers auth to a separate shared SKILL.md. Because authentication details are hidden in an external file (or created by a command), the actual credential requirements and token storage locations are unknown — this opacity could hide requests for OAuth tokens, stored credentials, or filesystem reads of auth material.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and is user-invocable. It does not request persistent system presence or modifications to other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other high privileges here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a thin wrapper around the gws CLI to manage Google Tasks, which is reasonable. However, it delegates authentication, global flags, and security rules to a ../gws-shared/SKILL.md file that is not included here — you should inspect that shared SKILL.md (or the output of `gws generate-skills`) before installing to know: (1) what OAuth scopes or tokens are required, (2) where credentials are stored on disk or in environment variables, and (3) whether any credentials might be sent to external endpoints. Also verify the provenance of the gws CLI binary (is it an official Google Workspace CLI?) and run the skill in an isolated/test environment until you confirm it only uses the expected Google Tasks APIs and stores tokens in locations you control. If you cannot review the referenced gws-shared auth file, treat this package as opaque and proceed cautiously.
